transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Federal aviation officials expect airline schedules to return to normal by tonight as
carriers work through the fallout from Friday's nationwide ground stop.
NPR's Mara Liasson reports passengers are still facing cancellations and delays while
airlines get planes and crews back into place.
Speaking to reporters yesterday, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said communication systems
work by a contractor was the culprit, not new AI tools or a cyber attack.
We don't believe this was cyber at all.
This was an FAA system that didn't meet the moment.
Duffy blamed Congress for not giving the FAA more money for upgrades, but Republicans who
are still in charge of Congress until January already approved $12.5 billion for safety
upgrades in the one big beautiful bill.
Democrats on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee say that the administration
has only spent $1 billion of those funds.
Meanwhile, President Trump hasn't spoken publicly or posted about the ground stop or the request
for more money.
Mara Liasson, NPR News.
A federal judge has temporarily blocked President Trump's plans to redevelop a public park and
golf course along the Potomac River in Washington, D.C., and PR's Kate Bartlett reports.
The judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work on the site, which had been due
to close on Sunday for 15 months while it was redeveloped.
Trump and avid golfer once to turn the historic site, East Potomac Golf Links, into a championship-level
golf course.
The plaintiffs in the case, including the D.C. Preservation League, argue the new course
would be unaffordable.
On Saturday, before the order, Trump said on social media that anyone in the D.C. area
would be given a 50 percent discount.
The development is just one of the president's planned projects in the nation's capital.
Kate Bartlett, NPR News.
Italy is finding tech giant META nearly $900 million for accessing Facebook users' photos
and videos stored on Android devices, Esme Nicholson reports.
Italy's data protection agency says META has violated European privacy directives by
failing to obtain specific consent and to properly inform users that its Facebook app
could access all photos and videos and the related metadata on Android devices.
The regulator says Facebook's access permissions were not transparent and users did not understand
what they were authorizing.
It has instructed META to seek consent with separate, specific and clear requests.
The authority also cited META's lack of cooperation during the investigation.
The fine comes to about 0.4 percent of META's annual turnover.
For MPR News, I'm Esme Nicholson in Berlin.
ArtNet started out in 1989 as an online database to provide info on art auction sales.
Last year, it was acquired by a venture capital firm, Beowulf Capital.
Now ArtNet says it will help Cauchy curate the markets that users can bet on.
Critics of the deal say that art auctions already take place in a high-stakes, insular
world and that the chances of market manipulation are steep.
Some are also saying it's going to make the art world even more focused on money, not
creative expression.
The partnership was announced soon before the annual wintertime art fairs like Miami
Art Week commence.
Anastasia Tsiolkas, NPR News.
The Philippines has won the first Asian edition of the Eurovision Song Contest.
19-year-old Carmel took the title Saturday in Bangkok with her dance pop song "Sober
Sobra."
The song celebrates female empowerment and pays tribute to Filipino women.
Artists from 11 countries competed in the final.
Thailand finished second, followed by Vietnam in third.
Viewers cast votes from more than 180 countries and territories around the world.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.
This message comes from NPR sponsor Charles Schwab.

Your biases can lead you astray.

topics.text: FAA communications contractor system failure causes nationwide ground stop; airlines work to restore schedules
Federal judge temporarily blocks Trump's redevelopment of East Potomac Golf Links park in Washington
Italy fines Meta nearly $900 million over Android photo and video access without proper consent
ArtNet partners with Cauchy to let users bet on art market outcomes, drawing manipulation criticism
Philippines wins first Asian Eurovision Song Contest with Carmel's song 'Sober Sobra' in Bangkok
